Review complete. Implementation traced against the real pathfinder source; all four merge-gate criteria hold. One minor test-accuracy finding. **What the diff does:** extracts the four/five `pathfinder.stop()` sites in `bot/src/index.js` into one `stopOnce()` helper that stops only a real path, cancels a stationary live goal with `setGoal(null)`, and otherwise does nothing — while still flipping `ctx.lastGoalKey` to `'idle'` for stop-once semantics. That is exactly what the bead asked for. Verification I ran: - `bot.pathfinder.goal` is a real getter over `stateGoal` (`mineflayer-pathfinder/index.js:104-108`), so the `else if` guard reads live plugin state. - `setGoal(null)` → `resetPath('goal_updated')` with `stopPathing` false, so it clears the goal without latching. - `stopPathing` is consumed only at node arrival (`:582`) or in `resetPath` (`:139`); both null `stateGoal`, so the `isMoving()` branch cannot leave a latch on an empty path. No reachable "empty path + latched flag" state. - No crash path: `setGoal(null)` reaching `stateMovements.clearCollisionIndex()` requires a goal to already exist, which requires movements to be set. - Branch pinning: deleting the `isMoving()` stop fails the no-target test (`stop === 1`); deleting the `setGoal(null)` branch fails `liveGoal === null`; making it unconditional fails `calls.setGoal === 2`; dropping the `lastGoalKey !== 'idle'` guard now fails the parked-stop test, since it forces `isMoving = () => true` before `ticker.stop()`. Both round-01 findings are genuinely fixed. - Scope is clean: two files, no renames, no deps, no hostnames or secrets.

findings.title: 'stop guard' test name claims a stationary live goal, but its mock never has one
findings.body:
The test is titled "idle after a stationary goal does not latch stop" and its comment on line 83 reads "goal never produced a path", but the mock replaces `setGoal` with a bare counter (lines 77-81) and never populates `bot.pathfinder.goal`, which `mockBot()` does not define either (lines 28-33). So on tick 2 `stopOnce()` evaluates `bot.pathfinder.goal` as `undefined` and takes neither branch — the scenario actually exercised is "empty path AND no goal", not "stationary live goal".

That makes the assertion `calls.setGoal === 2` (line 97) mock-specific rather than a property of the code: with the real plugin, `setGoal(new GoalFollow(...), true)` installs `stateGoal` (`mineflayer-pathfinder/index.js:142-146`, exposed by the getter at :104-108), the goal stays live while `isMoving()` is false because `dynamicGoal` suppresses the clear at :460, and the idle tick would therefore issue `setGoal(null)` — giving `calls.setGoal === 3` and `effectiveGoals === 3`.

The empty-path-no-goal case the test really covers is reachable and is merge-gate criterion 1, so the assertions are valid; the stationary-goal case is covered by the second test (lines 101-129). The defect is that a maintainer reading this test will believe the stationary-goal path is covered here and that it produces no `setGoal` call, which is the opposite of what the code does — the exact confusion round 01 was about. Pre-existing from the first commit of this branch, not introduced by the fix commit.
findings.fix: Rename the test to say what it tests — e.g. "idle with no live goal never stops, so the next follow is not swallowed" — and change the line 83 comment from "goal never produced a path" to note that the mock keeps `pathfinder.goal` unset (goal already reached/cleared, empty path). Leave the assertions as they are.
